title: Generated file-store traces: after these operations, are all goal conditions satisfied?
decision: whether, after an agent's numbered trace of set / delete / rename / copy / move steps on a small file store, every goal condition on the final tree holds (yes) or at least one fails (no)

source.name: generator build/gen_state_goal.py
source.version: gen_v4, 2026-10-08: true preamble (set creates or replaces; asserted for every step), ordinary file names and status words in five domains, goal-directed macro traces (deviations keep the trace macro-coherent), self-explaining deviation names, meta.level

licence: generated by the benchmark's script (no third-party text)
notes: 300 matched pairs: a trace that reaches the goal (yes) and the same item with one operation of the trace changed so that exactly one goal condition fails (no); the pair id is meta.pair, also the group. gen_v4: the preamble is true for every step (delete / rename / copy / move find their source file, set creates the file or replaces its content, every step changes the store), file names and contents are ordinary names and status words of five domains (meta.domain), traces are built from goal-directed macros (every trace, planted deviations included, can be cut into whole macros, so a deviation is a wrong choice inside valid macros), and the deviation kinds are named wrong_target (v0: wrong_key), wrong_content (wrong_value), steps_swapped (swap), step_missing (missing; 75 each; one unrelated single step is inserted so the length is unchanged). meta.failed_condition = the failing goal condition (1-based). meta.level 1 / 2 / 3 = meta.steps 5 / 15 / 25 (200 rows each); start size 6-8, 8-12, 11-15 files; goal of 3, 5, 7 conditions (exists, absent, content, count, same; each is sensitive to at least one step). State length 1514 to 4246 characters. Truth by simulation on the specification; recomputed by check(item) from the state text alone on a second data structure. Four layouts of the file list, four wordings of the goal, four step notations and four numberings, drawn per item.

sample.note: a sample of two whole contrast groups (one of level 1, one of level 3) for the tests of this repository; EVALUATION ONLY, never a training source
